summary: A cliff light on Vancouver Island's Pacific coast, lit in 1891 for ships entering Juan de Fuca Strait; keepers left in 2024 and the light runs automatically.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: 1891 is the first (wooden) tower; the present concrete tower was begun after a postponement noted in 1920-21 and completed in the year ended March 1923. Lighthouse Friends says 1922; some lists give 1920.

notes_for_editor: Story footnotes 1-14 match sources 1-14. Lighthouse Friends is the main narrative source (copyrighted; paraphrased). Dates disagree: present tower 1920 (some lists) vs 1922 (LHF) vs reports (postponed FY1921, completed FY ended Mar 1923). Etzkorn tenure: LHF 1986-at least 2013; Times Colonist 1979-2015; Wikipedia 1986-2016. Ted Daykin trip: LHF 'hunting', HikeWCT 'prospecting' (1893). Departmental report page numbers are printed pages from corpus grep; FY labels follow the corpus (year the fiscal year ends). The 1910 report table's station alignment for the diaphone plant is unclear in OCR, so the story says so. Keeper roster is LHF's list (no USLHS for Canada); 1900-1920s tables in marine_ca not matched. 2024 access status unverified: LHF predates withdrawal. A Facebook post claimed Parks Canada closed the grounds in late 2024; not used. Verification: 1910 report p.87 table is columnar (Triangle Island, Estevan Point, Carmanah); the diaphone plant is probably Carmanah's by position but the story keeps the hedge. LHF gives a fifth-order lens in 1909 but a third-order lens moved in 1922; unexplained, noted in story. Heritage record text for ownership not readable in cache; story claims only that a record exists.
